source.practice_formula: (current percent - attribute penalty + effective teacher percent) / 2

mage.strategy: Convert the single intellectual practice budget into reliable spell damage first, then buy travel safety only after the damage chain is usable.
mage.practice_policy: Reach evocation magiks 30% for chill touch, improve chill touch, and retain later intellectual practices for mana growth unless a listed damage or mobility priority is below target.
automation_gaps: Protective buffs remain deferred until pre-hunt casting, expiry, and recast handling are generic.

cleric.strategy: Unlock cause serious for direct damage, then buy efficient self-healing that can extend field segments while preserving a fixed mana reserve; add passive attacks and shield mitigation as teachers expose them.
cleric.practice_policy: Reach healing and harmful magiks 30%, cause light 30%, and cause serious first. Then raise cure light and cure serious to 30%; the combat controller permits at most two self-heals below 35% health while retaining 30% mana.
automation_gaps: Armor, protection, and sanctuary still need generic pre-hunt casting plus affect expiry and recast handling.
source_refs: server/src/magic.c: spell_cause_light, spell_cause_serious, spell_cure_light, and spell_cure_serious
server/src/const.c: Cleric spell mana and beat costs

thief.strategy: Buy passive attack frequency, complete the stealth gates for a high-damage backstab opener, then add recurring circle damage and weapon control.
thief.practice_policy: Raise stealth techniques to 60%, hide to 20%, and sneak to 40%; keep second attack and then backstab as physical throughput targets, then build the exact defense chain for disarm and armed/unarmed chains for circle.
automation_gaps: Backstab and circle depend on maintaining an accessible piercing or stabbing weapon.
source_refs: server/src/fight.c: do_backstab, do_circle, do_disarm, multi_hit, and check_dodge

warrior.strategy: Maximize ordinary combat rounds with extra attacks and weapon-hit multipliers, then build grip and disarm so armed opponents lose damage and weapon-dependent control.
warrior.practice_policy: Prioritize second attack, armed combat knowledge 40%, and enhanced damage. Then raise shield block, defense knowledge, dodge, parry, and grip through the exact disarm gates; use kick and later attacks whenever their earlier gates are satisfied.
automation_gaps: Later attack chains require class-teacher availability and live confirmation at their unlock levels.

psionic.strategy: Concentrate intellectual practices on the shortest direct-damage chain because the same unspent practice pool also increases next-level mana.
psionic.practice_policy: Raise mind thrust to 30%, telepathy disciplines to 45%, and psychic crush next; defer alternate disciplines until their combat command or buff lifecycle is implemented.
automation_gaps: Agitation, mental barrier, displacement, and psychic healing need source-verified command timing and autonomous use policies before they justify scarce intellectual practices.

shifter.strategy: Use normal-form passive attacks, dodge, and recovery for early leveling. Chameleon, hawk, and cat are utility forms; snake is the first form that creates a natural weapon but sits behind a long intellectual-practice chain.
shifter.practice_policy: Spend early physical practices on second attack, dodge, and fast healing. Preserve intellectual practices until a form controller can justify the group forms 40%, chameleon 40%, hawk 32%, cat 40%, and snake path without sacrificing excessive level-up mana.
automation_gaps: Snake-form weapon use, form-specific actions, legal equipment removal and restoration, mana reserve, travel behavior, and normal-form recovery require a dedicated form controller.
source_refs: server/src/sft.c: do_morph and early form implementations

brawler.strategy: Combine passive extra attacks and enhanced damage with punch as the first source-positive active maneuver. Defer headbutt because its two-round command lag and size, head, mount, and trauma restrictions make it a control tool rather than an early XP accelerator.
brawler.practice_policy: Reach combat knowledge 40% and second attack, then pugilism knowledge 40% and one punch lesson. Keep enhanced damage as the main physical target after punch is usable; revisit punch at 51% for second punch and continue enhanced hit when later teachers offer it.
automation_gaps: Second punch needs live unlock evidence; later grappling and control actions need target anatomy, trauma, position, and lag-aware policies.
source_refs: server/src/fight.c: multi_hit, one_hit, do_headbutt, and check_dodge

ranger.strategy: Build passive melee frequency and a source-backed opening bow volley, then extend the defensive chain through grip and disarm to suppress armed opponents.
ranger.practice_policy: Reach armed combat knowledge 20% for second attack. When a source-identified bow is equipped, reach archery knowledge 20% and improve shoot; otherwise preserve those practices. Then raise defense knowledge, dodge, parry, and grip through the exact disarm gates.
automation_gaps: The engine still needs a reusable bow acquisition and replacement policy; forage and dowse need terrain-aware success, retry, and inventory policies.

smithy.strategy: Exploit counterbalance as the first offensive crafting payoff because it permanently gives a weapon an extra-attack chance equal to the learned skill, while avoiding material-heavy upgrades during early leveling.
smithy.practice_policy: With a source-identified wielded weapon, reach weaponsmithing 10%, take one counterbalance lesson, apply it at the Midgaard smithy anvil, and then practise shield block; defer hurl until a replaceable weapon or shield is chained.
automation_gaps: Hurl still requires weaponchain or shieldchain plus safe in-combat item recovery; material-consuming weapon and armour upgrades need resource valuation and replacement policies.
source_refs: server/area/midgaard.are: room 3050 forge and anvil resets
